title: Inverted error handling logic
detail: The original code cleared the error only when `should_ignore_error(error)` was true. The new code clears the error when the condition is false, causing all errors to be suppressed unless `should_ignore_error` returns true, which is the opposite of the intended behavior.
note: Says errors are cleared when the condition is false, which the planted `not` does.

title: Incorrect dunder method check in ChainableUndefined
detail: The condition mistakenly checks that the name does not start with double underscores while ending with them, which never matches valid dunder names. This prevents AttributeError from being raised for unimplemented dunder methods, breaking protocol probing such as copy.copy.
note: Says the check of a name not starting with `__` never matches real dunders, which the planted `!=` does.

title: Incorrect condition for zero-with-exponent handling
detail: When `max_digits` is `None`, the expression `max_digits <= decimal_places` raises a TypeError because `None` cannot be compared to an int. This causes the function to crash on valid inputs where only `decimal_places` is set.
note: Names the comparison of a None `max_digits` with `<=`.

title: Incorrect logic for __Host- cookie validation
detail: The condition uses `not name.startswith("__host-")`, which causes all cookies with a __Host- prefix to be rejected regardless of their domain and path attributes. The intended logic should check that a __Host- cookie has a specified domain, a specified path, and that the path is exactly "/". As written, the function returns False for any __Host- cookie, breaking expected behavior.
note: Says `__Host-` cookies are always rejected, which the planted `and` does.

title: Incorrect index increment for trailing ZWJ
detail: When a zero‑width joiner is at the end of the string, the code adds 2 to index if index <= codepoint_count-1. If index is the second‑last code point, this skips the last code point entirely, producing wrong spans and potentially missing characters.
note: Describes the planted `<=`: a ZWJ second from the end steps the index past the last code point.
